channel.title: Ulix Knowledge Briefs
channel.description: Dated notes from Ulix Knowledge on books, research, archives, software, and other developments worth interpreting.

item.title: AI Is Solving Erdős Problems. Counting Them Is the Wrong Ruler.
item.description: The raw count is a bad benchmark. Some of the underlying mathematical results are stronger evidence than the score suggests.

item.title: Good Notes May Work Because They Show You What You Don't Understand
item.description: A new experiment suggests that useful notes may improve learning partly by making overconfidence harder to maintain.

item.title: The First Herculaneum Scroll We Can Read Without Opening
item.description: A sealed Herculaneum papyrus has been virtually unwrapped and read end to end while remaining physically rolled shut.

item.title: Memory Without Provenance Is a Liability
item.description: AI agents are learning to remember. The harder problem is preserving where those memories came from, what surrounded them, and how they changed.

item.title: You Read Differently When You Expect to Remember It
item.description: An eye-tracking study found that reading for study changes what readers actually do with a text. The useful lesson is not simply to read more slowly.

item.title: The Odyssey Is a Bestseller Again. That Is Not a Bad Way to Meet Homer.
item.description: Christopher Nolan's film has sent thousands of readers back to Homer. Whatever one thinks of the adaptation, that is a reasonably good result.
